_comment: Phase-3 WP5/WP6 typed records with FULL byte accounting: every byte of every record is a declared field or an explicit UNKNOWN span — typing never erases ignorance. Regenerate: tools/phase3_record_types.py (add --probe for the live domain/lifetime pass).

player_block.lifetime: Resident for the whole session; re-initialized at scene load and at respawn (respawn writes hp:=4 at the level spawn point, lives-1). Not pooled.

contact_record.lifetime: POOLED. Allocated by contact_alloc 0x80059E44 = round-robin FREE-SLOT search over the 64 slots with NO full-array escape: with every slot occupied the search never returns (capacity HANG, proven by callFunction A/B). Cursor 0x8008234C wraps at 0x40 and measures allocation churn, NOT overwrite-oldest. A slot is LIVE when lifetime_ttl(+0x22) > 0 AND flags(+0x33) & 0x02 (the walker gate, disassembled from FUNC_800586B0). RETIREMENT IS BY TTL EXPIRY: +0x22 counts down every logic tick and the slot goes dead at 0 - so contacts free themselves over time, which is why pristine play never approaches capacity. MOD-SAFETY: never hold all 64 slots (a mod that refreshes TTLs can).

actor_record.lifetime: Loaded AT SCENE LOAD from LEVEL.RAW chunk-31 (XYZ file<<5) into a FIXED table; records are not reallocated during play. Enemies additionally appear in the LIVE pointer table 0x80090748, which is COMPACTED when an actor is removed (observed: slots shift up on a kill) - so a live-table index is NOT a stable identity, the record address is. MOTION: one Level01 actor sample confirms velocity_x +0x1C and velocity_z +0x24 over 40 captured frames (19 moved frames; Z is clamped on 7). The retained artifact does not bank rejected Y candidates and therefore cannot support the former whole-campaign claim that actors have no stored Y velocity. Offset +0x20 remains unknown; do not name it from stride symmetry alone.

plant_slot.lifetime: POOLED with a cursor (0x800822B8, wraps at 0x14, skips occupied). Created by plant_spawn FUNC_8005BDBC 20-120 frames after the crack input; torn down 40-170 frames after an uproot input (type := 0). The seed RECORD is conserved across the whole cycle - it is raised +20480 while the plant lives and re-grounded at pinned X/Z on teardown.

camera_record.lifetime: DERIVED OUTPUT, not authoritative state. Written every logic tick by camera_follow_update 0x8004DF18: camera_pos exponentially chases camera_target, closing ~0.15 of the remaining gap per frame, and camera_target is itself RECOMPUTED each tick. PROVEN by poking each triple +50000: the position is pulled back toward the target (drift -39932 over 24 frames) and a poked target is recomputed away (drift -45425). A mod cannot move the camera by writing this struct - it must change the producer or the inputs the producer reads. Behavioral control (Phase 2): the struct provably moves under L1 and is static under no input.

render_descriptor_pointer_entry.lifetime: Fixed kind-to-descriptor pointer entries in resident BSS. Targets are shared and non-contiguous. Their strict-pristine post-load snapshots contain five scene-dependent byte offsets, so a consumer must follow the pointer and must not assume a target edit survives a transition. The responsible writer is not yet traced.

sfx_voice_slot.lifetime: Eight-slot SFX voice scheduler pool. A slot is free when voice_id is -1; the manager prefers the same descriptor, otherwise a free slot, and drops the request when no slot is available. This is original software ownership; the downstream 24 SPU hardware voices are a separate domain.

frontend_progress_record.lifetime: Resident frontend/bonus-progress command word. The exact initialization, retirement, and save interaction are not yet empirically closed; the structured ownership blocker below keeps those missing links visible.
